title: Schroedinger's Equation at 100: The Wave Picture That Helped and Possibly Hurt
summary: Schroedinger's equation gave early quantum theory a visual language that looked like physics again: a wave evolving by a linear differential equation. This essay argues that the same success also seeded a recurring impulse to keep quantum theory "classical-looking" by treating the wave function as a physical wave. Schroedinger quickly realized that, for many-particle systems, the wave function is naturally defined on configuration space rather than ordinary physical space, blocking any straightforward reading of it as a literal classical wave.
